articles.headline: NBA season tips off as Detroit stage epic 22-point comeback to defeat Celtics
keyFacts: The Detroit Pistons overcame a 22-point deficit to defeat the Boston Celtics 121-113 in their NBA season opener.
Cade Cunningham scored 22 points and had eight assists to help lead the Pistons to victory.
Paul George scored 38 points in his debut for the Celtics, setting a record for the most points by a Celtic in a debut.
body: NBA: Detroit Pistons stage epic 22-point comeback to defeat Boston Celtics as season tips off in style
Detroit Pistons rally from 22-points down to beat Boston Celtics 121-113 with Javonte Green and Cade Cunningham’s 22 points and 8 assists winning the day at Little Caesars Arena
Tuesday 20 October 2026 23:19, UK

Detriot Pistons staged an epic 23-0 run in the fourth quarter as they overcame a 22-point deficit - the largest come-from-behind win against the Boston Celtics in the last 30 seasons - to seal a stunning 121-113 win.

Javonte Green scored 19 points after not playing in the first half and Cade Cunningham finished with 22 points and eight assists, helping the Pistons to victory as the NBA season tipped off in style on Tuesday.

Paul George scored 38 points, the most by a Celtic in his debut. The nine-time All-Star, in his 17th season, showed he's still got it in his first game with Boston since it acquired him from Philadelphia in exchange for 2024 NBA Finals MVP Jaylen Brown.

articles.headline: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases
keyFacts: Madison County detectives solved the 1993 murder of Randy Gail Sperino using genetic genealogy and artificial intelligence.
Investigators sent DNA evidence to the company Othram, which used extended relative profiles to help identify Albert Buddy Zigler, who confessed and was charged.
Detectives also used an artificial intelligence platform to analyze over 2,000 pages of records, reconstruct timelines, and organise witness information.
body: - Published
Randy Gail Sperino was last seen alive on the evening of 9 November 1993, as she was getting into a pickup truck in Granite City, Illinois.
The 34-year-old's body was found hours later in a field nearby, the victim of blunt force trauma.
The identity of her killer was a mystery. DNA evidence found at the crime scene was tested against standard law enforcement databases, but no matches were found.
For three decades, investigators from the Madison County Sheriff's Office chased leads and interviewed hundreds of people as they attempted to identify the perpetrator.
The case looked like it would remain one of more than 250,000 unsolved homicides in the US.

Then, last year, detectives tried a fresh approach. They sent genetic evidence to Othram, a Houston-based company that uses DNA technology to help identify the perpetrators in cold and current crime cases.

The Madison County detectives had been inspired by investigative genetic genealogy techniques used to identify the Golden State Killer, Joseph James DeAngelo, back in 2018. In that case, an investigative team constructed a family tree to help identify the killer.
They were able to do so thanks to DNA data that relatives had provided to commercial databases, similar to consumer ancestry platforms.

Unlike traditional forensic DNA testing, which generally relies on a direct comparison between evidence and a known person, investigative genetic genealogy can identify distant genetic relatives of an unknown individual.

Othram set about applying this technique to track down Sperino's killer. While the killer's own DNA profile wasn't available, profiles submitted by his extended relatives allowed the company to identify a male family member.
"That lead broke the case open," said Captain Tim Lawrence of Madison County Sheriff's Office, which was responsible for investigating the crime.
It was a crucial clue that led the detectives to Albert "Buddy" Zigler, 70, who then confessed to the murder. He was charged in May this year.
Wes Sperino, Gail's son, said at a press conference: "I finally get closure and I finally know who did this."
The technique that led detectives to Zigler is credited with revolutionising how forensic cases are solved.
It has been highly successful in helping solve cases involving unidentified human remains and identifying suspects in longstanding investigations.

Othram claims it has helped solve thousands of cases. The company's chief executive David Mittelman likens investigative genetic genealogy to a GPS system: "The DNA profile is the GPS signal and it says 'you belong here.' But to understand where 'here' is, you need a map."
Public records, obituaries, and census data build that map so Othram's scientists can establish how different family trees connect.
However, Mittelman is quick to point out that DNA technology can only go so far before "a cascade of investigative steps" are needed.
DNA science isn't the only technology that are helping detectives solve cold cases.
One of the challenges facing detectives on major cases investigations like the hunt for Sperino's killer is the sheer amount of evidence they dig up.
Officers investigating Sperino's murder realised AI could help them wade through the mountains of evidence they had accumulated since 1993.

They used a platform called Centerline AI, from Florida software company CentralSquare, to analyse more than 2,000 pages of records and identify evidence for the DNA testing that helped to break the case.

The AI helped them reconstruct timelines and organise witness information. "It's so much easier than having a detective have to read through 2,000 pages," Lawrence says. His team could interact with the AI like a chat bot.
This also helped when it came to interviewing Zigler after they had tracked him down. Detectives were able to ask questions of the AI to help "figure out if Zigler was being truthful", says Lawrence.

But the technology is "only as good as the investigator," says the captain. There comes a point, he says, "where you leave the technology behind and you have to go track people down and talk to them."
Investigative genetic genealogy has its limitations too. Mittelman says: "It can't solve every case. If you have no DNA, you can't really use this technique."
"But this technique is a lot more powerful and a lot more likely to yield identities than having to rely on the chance that you find a match somewhere in a database," he adds.
While firms like Othram only use ancestry platforms where users have provided consent for law enforcement matching, there remain some concerns about the ethical implications of using this data.

"There are significant privacy concerns," says Denise Syndercombe Court, professor of forensic genetics at King's College London. While one person may have opted in to their DNA being used, genetic relatives may not have given consent.
A lack of funding is another hurdle. Mittelman says: "Every law enforcement agency wants to do it. There's just not a lot of funding for it."
Sometimes cases are funded through donations or crowdfunding. Othram operates a website listing cases that members of the public can help fund.

While investigative genetic genealogy has been adopted in countries such as Sweden, Denmark and Australia, it is not yet used in the UK. The Home Office is conducting a study to consider whether it should be adopted in the UK but did not respond to a request for comment.

The UK is already in a strong position, says Syndercombe Court. "We have such an efficient DNA database that if you can get any DNA out of a crime scene, you've got over a 65% chance of putting a name to that person, which is enormously powerful," she says.

articles.headline: Jayson Tatum & Paul George-led Celtics get roasted after blowing 22-point lead in loss to Pistons
keyFacts: The Boston Celtics blew a 22-point lead and lost 121-113 to the Detroit Pistons in their regular-season opener.
Celtics player Paul George scored a team-high 38 points in his debut, while Jayson Tatum scored 13 points on 6-of-23 shooting.
Celtics fans criticized the team and coach Joe Mazzulla on social media following the loss.
body: A huge belief among Boston Celtics fans was that a huge change was going to come, one way or another. Coach Joe Mazzulla led this team to a perfect 4-0 NBA preseason record, which sparked a lot of optimism. Then came opening night against the Detroit Pistons. Everything started out well, but Paul George and Jayson Tatum couldn't handle Cade Cunningham and Co.'s production. The result? A blown 22-point lead, a 121-113 loss, and a whole lot of declarations about the Celtics on social media.
Celtics led by Tatum and George get roasted amid blowing 22-point lead to Pistons

The Celtics steamrolled the Pistons to start their NBA season. They led 28-27 by the end of the first quarter. By the end of the second quarter, that lead had ballooned to about 22 points.But, as they say, 'it's not over until the fat lady sings.' Cade Cunningham helped his team score 76 points in just the second half alone.

The Celtics? Well, the squad led by Jayson Tatum and Paul George could only muster up 55 points. When the buzzer rang, the Celtics started off their regular season campaign with an L on the win-loss column.
NBA and Celtics fans were not having it. They immediately took to social media and expressed a whole lot of emotions.

"Same stuff. Different year. "Let's build a 20-some-point lead and see if the opponent can actually catch us. We'll do absolutely nothing to assist their comeback." NOTHING has changed. At all," a Celtics fan declared.

Another avid NBA spectator had Tatum and Coach Joe Mazzulla to blame, "This was a bad Tatum performance. He’ll be better. Who won’t be better is Mazzulla. He is such a bad in-game coach. He doesn’t know how to stop runs. Get away from live by/die by 3’s. Make defensive changes. Gonna be a long season with Mazz."

True enough, it was not really the best performance from the Celtics superstar. In a team-high 38 minutes, he scored only 13 points on 6-of-23 shooting. It didn't help that Tatum went 0% from the three-point line on seven attempts. He tried to affect the game in other ways, but his 11 assists and four rebounds weren't enough to keep them afloat against the Pistons.

Celtics fans did warm up to one bright spot during this loss. Paul George went ballistic. He scored 38 points on 57.1% from the field while shooting 58.3% from three-point range. This was the most points scored in a Celtics debut. He also dropped three assists to help their offense.
Paul George in his Celtics debut 🤯: 38 PTS (!!) 5 REB 3 AST 5 STL (!!) 78% TS Still got alot left in the tank https://t.co/Rn85dY3xIE
— Polymarket Hoops (@PolymarketHoops) October 20, 2026

Defensively, George also shined. He helped the Celtics by grabbing five rebounds while also snagging five steals. Some NBA fans even think this could be an MVP-level campaign in the making if sustained.

"If you have a real job or are a real person and couldn’t watch a 3:00 PM NBA game on a Tuesday don’t worry ….. You only missed Paul George announcing his MVP candidacy, first halves not mattering, and Ausar Thompson getting a new nickname," they wrote.
While a lot of huge statements dropped during this Celtics loss to the Pistons, some cool heads kept their optimism from getting lost amid all the negative emotions.

"I don’t think people understand that it’s a long season and it takes teams a bit to find their collective personality. That can’t happen in the pre-season. We saw what they want, but the path there goes through playing games. Celtics are fine," the fan posted.
Overreactions are normal during the start of the NBA regular season. Whether the Celtics dispel these narratives will depend on Coach Mazzulla, George, and Tatum.

articles.headline: Mike Perry confirms he's leaving BKFC behind for MMA: 'I'm going to give it my best shot'
keyFacts: Mike Perry confirmed he is permanently leaving bare-knuckle boxing after six undefeated appearances and the King of Violence title with BKFC.
Perry plans to focus on MMA for the foreseeable future, expecting to compete in the sport for at least the next two years.
Perry sustained a partial labral tear in his shoulder during an August fight against Brandon Jenkins but does not require surgery.
body: Mike Perry is moving on from bare-knuckle boxing.

Since leaving the UFC in 2021, Perry has essentially been the poster boy for bare-knuckle combat — more specifically, Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship (BKFC). However, after returning to the MMA world with two gloved bouts since May, Perry confirmed on Tuesday's edition of "The Ariel Helwani Show" that his time with BKFC is over.

"It's good to get that out. I kind of had some feelings about it," Perry told Uncrowned. "It's like the 'BK cheat code,' man. That bare-knuckle stuff is like a cheat code, I guess. Those two-minute rounds, I was good at it. It was fun. I made some noise doing it, and I'm ready for another challenge.
"So, I think MMA is in my foreseeable future, and I'm going to give it my best shot."

Perry, 35, has been primarily fixated on the art of gloveless combat for most of the past five years and has found great success. "Platinum" went undefeated in his six BKFC appearances, culminating in winning the promotion’s "King of Violence" title after defeating former UFC champions Eddie Alvarez and Luke Rockhold.

At MVP’s debut MMA event on Netflix this past May, Perry competed in MMA for the first time since his final UFC fight against Daniel Rodriguez in April 2021. Perry scored a second-round doctor's stoppage TKO win over seasoned veteran Nate Diaz in a lopsided affair , before he took on Brandon Jenkins on short notice at Duel: Arena in August.

Unfortunately for Perry, he suffered a shoulder injury mid-fight with Jenkins , leading to a first-round stoppage loss. Nonetheless, Perry said Tuesday that he expects to be back in the MMA world for at least the next two years, as he teased his next move without sharing details just yet.
"I'm going to give something a good shot here,” Perry said, “and just a couple years, at least I won't be going back [to BKFC], then I got some fights I'll have to focus on.”

Perry’s injury against Jenkins appeared to be a dislocated shoulder in the moment, and it effectively was. Perry noted that he sustained a partial labral tear, which caused the joint to pop out during an exchange with Jenkins on the ropes.
Perry doesn't expect to need surgery, as his doctors told him the muscles around the partial tear are still strong and supporting the area well.

"It was hard to go through, I guess. I'm doing OK," Perry said. "I was just at training [today], sparring with the guys. I got some rounds in. Still not doing as many rounds as I want, but that's not because of the shoulder. That's more like, I don't know, I'm slowly building. I'm super humble now. The game has humbled me, and I thought I was on this — I was trying to be great, and it's like, I saw these things: You wouldn't have moved if I didn't give you something to make you.
"So now it's like, kind of less pressure. I just want to be my healthiest, be my best, and people can say what they want to me. I don't want to get too angry about anything anymore.
"I was trying to calm down when my shoulder went out in the ring," Perry added. "I was trying to let them pull on it, and it just didn't seem to feel better anywhere."

Heading into Duel: Arena, Perry was supposed to face Dillon Danis. Or at least, he was until Danis withdrew two days out from fight night . The withdrawal was just another among several in Danis' combat sports career.

Despite that checkered history, Perry still believed throughout the build-up that he and Danis would fight. Now that they didn't, he’s trying his best to refrain from carrying animosity. Yet Perry also said that if he sees Danis, it won't be a friendly encounter.

"There's no professional business being done between me and that guy. I was upset with that guy," Perry said. "But maybe I shouldn't be, right? Like I said, I've got to learn to take things with a grain of salt.

"Everyone said he was going to do that. I was like, 'No way, no way, no way. He's coming, he's coming.' But he didn't dig into me in a nasty way and then not show up, with his trash talk and this and that. So, I can't be upset about stuff I can't control.

"You never know what's going to happen tomorrow," Perry continued. "Yesterday is history, tomorrow's a mystery, and today is a gift, or something like that. So, see, I don't want to snitch on myself prior to anything that could happen.

“Is he supposed to wrestle for RAF [this Friday]? I could go viral and go down there. These are thoughts I have, but I'm not going to do it. But if I saw Dillon Danis, we’ve gotta fight in the street. We’ve just gotta have a fight at this point, for free. Any parking lot. If I took a pay cut [to fight Jenkins after Danis withdrew], I'll pay cut myself. ... If I see him, we gotta squabble, bro."

articles.headline: Shrek 2 Remastered Officially Announced With Must-See GTA 6-inspired Trailer
keyFacts: Aspyr announced Shrek 2 Remastered with a trailer styled after Grand Theft Auto 6 marketing.
The remaster launches on November 10 for Nintendo Switch, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, Windows PC, and Xbox Series X.
The updated game features 4K resolution, improved textures, and new online co-op for up to four players.
body: Rockstar Games has spent years building hype for Grand Theft Auto 6, with every trailer and update becoming a major event for fans. But what if that same dramatic treatment was applied to a very different kind of video game? One starring a certain green ogre, perhaps?

That's apparently the thinking behind the official reveal of Shrek 2 Remastered, which has officially been announced with a trailer that channels nothing less than the cinematic style of Rockstar's GTA 6 marketing.

Developed by Aspyr, Shrek 2 Remastered will launch on Nov. 10 for Nintendo Switch, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, Windows PC, and Xbox Series X. The game first surfaced last month through an achievement leak, followed by an early Xbox Store listing that revealed details about its upgrades.
What to expect from Shrek 2 Remastered

Originally developed by Luxoflux and published by Activision, Shrek 2 is an action-adventure platformer based on DreamWorks Animation's hit 2004 film. Players travel through locations including Shrek's swamp, Fiona's castle and the kingdom of Far Far Away, revisiting scenes from the movie alongside additional sequences created for the game.

Players can control Shrek and other familiar characters, including Fiona and Donkey, as they fight enemies and tackle platforming challenges. The original game also supported cooperative play, letting up to four players join in locally.

The remaster brings the game to modern hardware with improved textures, an enhanced user interface, upgraded cutscenes and 4K resolution. It also adds a Photo Mode and a Cheat Mode that lets players modify their experience. Perhaps the biggest addition is online co-op. While the original supported local multiplayer, the remaster will let up to four players team up online.
The timing also makes sense from a franchise perspective. Shrek 5 is expected to arrive in 2027, giving fans a chance to revisit the series' early-2000s heyday before the ogre returns to theaters.

articles.headline: Judge dismisses Sam Altman’s sister’s sexual abuse lawsuit
keyFacts: US District Judge Zachary Bluestone dismissed the lawsuit filed by Ann Altman against her brother, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman.
The judge wrote that Ann Altman failed to appear for an independent medical examination and missed other deadlines.
The case was dismissed with prejudice, meaning it cannot be refiled, while a request for attorney fees was denied.
body: On Tuesday, US District Judge Zachary Bluestone dismissed the lawsuit Ann Altman filed last year alleging that her brother, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, had sexually abused her throughout her childhood. As reported earlier by The Guardian, the judge wrote that over the last year, Ann had failed to appear for an independent medical examination or meet other deadlines, despite warnings that it would result in the case being dismissed.
Judge dismisses Sam Altman’s sister’s sexual abuse lawsuit
Ann Altman’s lawsuit against her brother was dismissed with prejudice, meaning it can’t be refiled.

When the case was filed last year, a statement shared by Sam Altman, his mother, and his brothers said, “Annie has made deeply hurtful and entirely untrue claims about our family, and especially Sam… All of these claims are utterly untrue. This situation causes immense pain to our entire family.”

Judge Bluestone granted Sam Altman’s motion to dismiss the case with prejudice, meaning it can’t be refiled in that court, while denying Sam’s request for attorney fees and costs. Santos Perez, a lawyer who had represented Ann until withdrawing this month, told The Guardian in a statement that “I am no longer authorized to comment on this case but I continue to believe in Annie.”

articles.headline: No jeopardy but loads of fun - Champions League sets new goals record
keyFacts: The current Champions League season has set a record with 187 goals scored at an average of 4.16 per game.
Football analysts stated that the new 36-team format and lack of early jeopardy encourage teams to play more expansively.
Highlights will be broadcast on BBC iPlayer, the BBC Sport app, and BBC One.
body: - Published
More teams, more games - and more goals.
Since the current Champions League format was introduced at the start of the 2024-25 season, Europe's elite club competition has delivered all of the above and more.
Especially the goals part.
Already trending upwards over the past two campaigns, there has been a genuine goals boom in this year's competition.
The 187 goals scored so far have come at an average of 4.16 per game - the highest in Champions League history.
"Look how many goals have been scored, it's phenomenal," ex-Manchester United and England winger Ashley Young said on BBC Radio 5 Live. "The attackers are being clinical."
Former Liverpool defender Stephen Warnock described the volume of goals as "incredible" - so how unusual is it?
What the stats say
Ready for lots of numbers?
Not only is the current goals-per-game percentage the highest ever in the Champions League, it is the third highest in European Cup history - behind only 1959-60 (4.19) and 1955-56 (4.38).
While 40 goals were scored across nine games on Tuesday, last week was even more spectacular.
Last Wednesday saw the third highest-scoring day in Champions League history (46 goals), bettered only by the final league-phase matchdays of 2024-25 and 2025-26, when 18 matches took place.
The 78 goals scored across Tuesday and Wednesday last week made matchday two the highest scoring in history.
That was nine more than the total scored on matchday one this season (69) - which, at the time, was the second highest-scoring matchday since the new league phase was introduced in 2024-25.
Will we see the record fall again this week? It's already halfway there.
More entertainment = more quality?

Ever since Uefa announced its plans to alter the format of the Champions League in 2021, the impact on matches has been a hot topic. Scrutiny has only increased since the changes were implemented in time for the 2024-25 season.
After beginning life as a six-team invitational tournament in 1955-56 before growing to a 32-team knockout tournament in 1967, the Champions League as we know it began in 1992.

A group stage was added, with the last 16 entering a knockout phase. There was a brief spell with two group stages, but this was reverted back to the single group-stage format for the 2003-04 tournament.
The group stage previously featured 32 teams in eight groups of four, with the top two sides from each of those groups qualifying for the last 16.
For the start of the 2024-25 season, the group stage was replaced with a 36-team league phase, with each side playing eight one-off fixtures instead of six games against three teams.
The top eight finishers qualify directly for the knockout stages, with those placed ninth to 24th entering a two-legged play-off stage.

The bottom eight are eliminated, meaning that after eight matches, 24 sides are still in the competition. Some argue that that creates a lack of jeopardy, which encourages teams to play more expansively.
But do more goals equal better quality?
"I think the entertainment has gone up, although I'm not sure the quality has gone up," The Times football writer Tom Arnott told BBC Radio 5 Live.
"If I'm looking at the games it's brilliant to watch and thrilling because the football itself is fantastic - but what do they mean?

"The lack of jeopardy, why would PSG and Barcelona play for a draw, why not go for it? If you need five wins from the eight games you know you've got some margin there. If you lose it's OK. I think the format allows all the teams to loosen up.
"The entertainment value is there but I think you come away from these matches sometimes and still think 'what does it all mean?'. The lack of jeopardy early on does deliver entertainment."
Watch highlights of every Champions League game from 22:00 on Wednesday on BBC iPlayer and the BBC Sport website and app.
There will also be a Champions League Match of the Day on BBC One on Wednesday, from 22:40 to 00:00.

articles.headline: Anthropic pitches AI safety bill that may block a model if 50+ people could be killed
keyFacts: TechCrunch reported that AI lab Anthropic is circulating a draft bill for congressional consideration that proposes blocking AI models under certain catastrophic risk scenarios.

Politico stated that the legislation suggests independent evaluators registered with the U.S. Commerce Department analyze models for potential disasters involving 50 or more deaths or a billion dollars in damage.
An Anthropic spokesperson told Politico that the draft bill reflects proposals from the company's Advanced AI Framework, which it has advocated for since June.
body: Over the past year, concerns have swirled over the potential dangers posed by artificial intelligence, and debates have raged over the proper path for AI safety. Now, Anthropic appears to have put forth its own vision for how the government might regulate its industry.

Politico recently reported that the AI lab has been shopping around a new draft bill on AI safety that it hopes Congress might consider adopting. The legislation posits certain scenarios in which the release of an AI model could be blocked from distribution.

Those scenarios involve a “foreseeable, imminent risk” — one in which over 50 people are at risk of dying or if over a billion dollars in property damage could result, Politico writes. The catastrophic risk in question must “stem from the creation or release of a biological weapon, the model evading its developer’s controls or a cyberattack,” the outlet notes.

The metrics offered here — 50 people and a billion dollars — are similar to those in a piece of California legislation that was recently passed into law, Senate Bill 53, which similarly defined those scenarios as tantamount to “catastrophic risk.”

Anthropic’s bill suggests that analysis of a model’s potential for disaster could be arrived at via the use of “independent evaluators” who would be registered with the U.S. Commerce Department. These evaluators could potentially be paid by the AI labs themselves — so long as the “payment is not contingent on the evaluations’ results,” Politico writes.

It’s not clear how this proposed system would assure that payments couldn’t influence the evaluation. Demis Hassabis, chairman of DeepMind, posited some months ago that a self-governing AI regulatory body should mimic the financial industry’s Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA).

In Anthropic’s draft bill, when evaluators determine that an imminent catastrophic risk is posed, they would have 72 hours to contact the Commerce Department about it. The Commerce Department would then have to request to a D.C. judge to halt the model’s release. The legislation would expressly forbid any federal agency from having the discretion to halt the model’s distribution on its own, Politico writes.

Anthropic did not immediately respond to TechCrunch’s a request for comment but a spokesperson did confirm the draft bill to Politico. “This bill represents the proposals outlined in Anthropic’s Advanced AI Framework, which we have been advocating for with federal and state lawmakers since June,” the spokesperson said.

The theoretical risks offered in the draft policy are a little bit far afield from the kinds of incidents that have been top of mind for the tech industry of late. While there are people warning of the potential of human death, the primary concern has largely been the threat of agentic hacking. A rash of incidents in which AI programs have apparently disobeyed their human operators and hacked websites on the open internet has spurred concern that models may be lacking proper security controls.
In an effort to present a solution to the spectacle of crisis that the labs themselves have helped bring about, companies like Anthropic have offered up their own preferred solutions.

Indeed, despite labs’ perpetual warnings that the technology they’re selling could result in the demise of human civilization, they have largely been resistant to mandatory government oversight. Instead, they have suggested a voluntary system of embedded evaluators — supposedly “neutral” third-party observers that are placed inside AI organizations so that they can monitor the models for potential signs of risk or abuse.

Still, Anthropic’s mere suggestion for legislation appears to go slightly further than others’ regulatory proposals offered by the industry, including Nvidia, who’s CEO Jensen Huang recently argued that the AI industry didn’t need any new laws at all.

articles.headline: The Chronicles of Narnia Books are on Sale at Amazon, Including a Deluxe Edition Hardcover
keyFacts: Amazon is offering a buy one, get one 50 percent off promotion on Chronicles of Narnia books this week.
The sale applies to hardcovers, paperbacks, box sets, and a deluxe edition, with discounts automatically applied in the cart.
Greta Gerwig's Narnia movie is scheduled to release in theaters on February 12, 2027, and on Netflix in April 2027.
body: Amazon is currently running a buy 1, get 1 50% off sale on all of the Narnia books this week. The promotion extends to hardcovers, box sets, paperbacks, and even a massive 7-in-1 deluxe edition. With Greta Gerwig's upcoming Narnia movie hitting theaters early next year, this discount is a great time to read the original C.S. Lewis novels that inspired it all.

If you're only looking to read the source material for Gerwig's movie, you'll want to check out the deal on The Magician's Nephew first. The paperback, hardcover, and collector's edition are included in the sale. You can also get a copy of it in the box set or deluxe edition available here if you want the full collection instead.
Buy 1, Get 1 Half Off Narnia Book Sale at Amazon

Amazon has these types of sales pretty regularly and now is a particularly good time to buy multiple books at once . All you need to do is add two eligible books to your cart and Amazon will automatically apply the 50% discount to whichever one is the cheapest. This means you'll want to buy two similarly priced books to take full advantage of the discount.

So, for example, if you're looking to buy the deluxe edition at $39.50, you probably don't want to also buy The Magician's Nephew paperback for $7 at the same time. Instead you'll want to browse the sale for something closer to $40 to maximize your savings. Because of that, this sale usually works best if you're looking to get multiple copies of the same book at the same price point.
Where Is The Magician's Nephew on the Book Timeline?

If you're new to The Chronicles of Narnia books , it's worth noting that the official reading order is up for debate. If you're looking to read the story in terms of when the events take place chronologically, The Magician's Nephew would count as book one in the series. But it was actually the fifth book C.S. Lewis published. The box set and the deluxe edition both place The Magician's Nephew as the first book, but it may not be the order you'll want to read it in.

The actual order in which you read the books doesn't really matter, and C.S. Lewis has said as much . But if you're a purist who would rather read the books in the way Lewis intended his audience to read them at the time, you'll want to start with The Lion, The Witch, and The Wardrobe instead.
When Is the New Chronicles of Narnia Movie Coming Out?

It's been in the works for a while, but Greta Gerwig's Narnia movie is coming to theaters pretty soon. It's theatrical debut is set for February 12, 2027 and it will eventually come directly to Netflix in April 2027. So if you want to read the book before seeing the movie, you've still got some time to do so.

articles.headline: Oura Ring can track new stats related to cardio fitness
keyFacts: Smart ring company Oura announced that it is adding two new fitness features called Cardio Effort and VO2 Max.
Cardio Effort uses five ranges to assess weekly body strain compared to an individual baseline, according to the company.

body: Oura Ring can track new stats related to cardio fitness
The smart rings are getting Cardio Effort and VO2 Max data.

Smart ring company Oura announced that it is adding two new fitness features. First is Cardio Effort, an assessment of how much strain the wearer has put on their body during activity. The personalized metric will offer five ranges — light, fair, maintaining, building and reaching — that offer a gauge of how the week's activities compare to the individual's baseline. The feature is based on the Training Impulse method and is designed to monitor long-term trends in cardiovascular activity, the company said.

The second feature is that the smart rings will automatically estimate VO2 Max stats. This feature was previously called Cardio Capacity in the Oura Labs tool. It wasn't an automatic metric and it required a six-minute walking test before it could be enabled. The revised VO2 Max makes passive estimations on regular GPS-enabled workouts, meaning the test is no longer needed. VO2 Max stats will be available in Oura Labs for the third-generation Oura Ring and later models.

These new additions further expand Oura's offerings for holistic health data. Other wearables, including the Apple Watch and Fitbit, have been able to track similar cardio metrics for some time, so the change could make Oura a viable option for people who prefer the ring form factor to the watch or bracelet ones.

articles.headline: The Gambia to pay reparations to ex-dictator’s victims from sale of US mansion
keyFacts: Gambian authorities announced that funds from the sale of former President Yahya Jammeh's US mansion will pay reparations to his victims.

body: Gambian authorities have announced that funds from the sale of the country’s former president’s mansion in the United States would be used to pay reparations to victims of his rule.

The Gambia Reparations Commission confirmed Tuesday that it received just more than $2.5m from the sale of a property in the wealthy Washington, DC suburb of Potomac, Maryland, belonging to ex-President Yahya Jammeh.

The commission, which was set up to compensate victims of abuses committed during Jammeh’s 22-year rule ending in 2017, said in a statement that “the funds were deposited directly into the Reparations Fund account at the Central Bank of The Gambia and shall only be utilized for the payment of reparations”.
“The Commission is committed to ensuring that the funds are managed responsibly, transparently and accountably, with due regard to the rights and needs of victims and survivors,” it added.
Jammeh currently lives in Equatorial Guinea, after he was forced out under pressure from The Gambia’s West African neighbours following his 2016 election loss to current President Adama Barrow.
He is accused of presiding over the murder of political opponents, disappearances, rape and torture.
A commission of inquiry estimated that between 240 and 250 victims were killed by Jammeh’s forces in the former British colony of two million people.
Proceeds from corruption
President Barrow said in a statement that his government would heed any recommendations by official auditors on how the funds would be allocated to victims.
The US Justice Department filed a civil forfeiture complaint in 2020 alleging that the property was bought with proceeds of corruption. A court ordered its forfeiture in 2022.
The property, it asserted, was purchased through a trust set up by Jammeh’s wife.
The US Justice Department had announced in September that it would return the funds from the mansion sale to The Gambia.

articles.headline: Hegseth points to Starshield ‘terms of service’ in Ukraine speed cap dispute
keyFacts: War Secretary Pete Hegseth suggested Starshield speed caps affecting Ukraine may stem from terms of service violations rather than government directives.
The communication slowdown hampered Ukraine's drone operations, while Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky alleged a political decision caused the disruption.
Hegseth also denied claims by Zelensky that the War Department is withholding deliveries of Patriot interceptor missiles to Ukraine.
body: War Secretary Pete Hegseth on Tuesday suggested a violation of Starshield’s terms of service could have led to the speed of the communication systems used by Ukraine being throttled.

The Cabinet official’s comments come as conflicting accounts have emerged over who ordered a slowdown of Starshield, the military version of Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite network developed by SpaceX under contract with the War Department and used by Ukraine in its war against Russia .
“We haven’t pulled anything back,” Hegseth said. “There are terms of service that ultimately need to be complied to, and that’s where Starlink has the option to make those decisions.”
“Nothing’s changed from our view,” the secretary said. “We haven’t made any directives or anything like that, and we wish the Ukrainians obviously success.”

Musk, President Donald Trump , and other administration officials have faced questions over who authorized the restrictions, which have hampered Ukraine’s ability to operate drones used in offensive missions and to intercept Russian attacks.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has been blunt about who he believes is responsible for the disruptions, saying, “All of this suggests that some political decision has been made to slow down support for us.”

Zelensky had initially demanded Musk address the issue when it first arose, but the SpaceX founder pointed out that Starshield is owned and operated by the U.S. government. Trump has also maintained he did not impose speed restrictions on Ukraine’s access to Starshield.

The Wall Street Journal reported Tuesday that Musk personally ordered the slowdown last week, citing U.S. officials familiar with the matter. The decision reportedly blindsided Ukrainian officials and created confusion within the Trump administration. Musk and Trump discussed the restrictions before and after they were imposed, the outlet reported.

Hegseth also disputed on Tuesday Zelensky’s claim that the war secretary is withholding the delivery of more Patriot interceptor missiles for Ukraine’s air defense system despite NATO already paying for them.

“There’s a lot of things that have been said in the press that are not true about the Department of War,” Hegseth said. “We haven’t changed our posture in any way towards the Ukrainians. But certainly, with things like interceptors — we want to make sure our guys have the most possible.”
ZELENSKY SAYS HEGSETH BLOCKING MISSILES, STILL ‘NO EXPLANATION’ FOR STARSHIELD LIMITS

Ukraine has depleted its stock of U.S.-made Patriot interceptors, leaving the country susceptible to aerial attacks from Russia. Zelensky placed the blame directly on Hegseth for the delayed arrival of the interceptors during a virtual meeting with a bipartisan group of U.S. senators.

The dispute over Ukrainian defense needs comes as tensions boil between Washington and Kyiv over Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy infrastructure. Trump has criticized the attacks on Russian refineries, blaming them for contributing to rising fuel prices, while Ukrainian officials have defended their military operations as necessary to counter Moscow’s aggression.

articles.headline: Investigation Reveals How TikTok Executives Ignored Internal Child-Safety Warnings
keyFacts: Court documents from an ongoing multistate trial reveal that TikTok executives repeatedly ignored internal staff warnings regarding child safety and age restrictions.
The NPR report states that underage users accessed adult features like live video streaming, with TikTok reportedly profiting from the sexual exploitation of minors.
A TikTok spokesperson stated that the NPR report cherry-picked information to mislead the public and ignored documents demonstrating the company's youth safety commitments.
body: Court documents on some of the inner workings of TikTok paint a picture of a tech company repeatedly warned by its own staff about the dangers its platform posed to minors — and then ignoring many of those warnings.

According to an investigation from NPR, unsubmitted depositions from an ongoing multistate trial against TikTok, Meta, Google and Snap reveal that TikTok executives knew that underage users were circumventing its age restrictions. Internal documents also reportedly show that some minors were engaging in sexually exploitative acts using TikTok’s own platform features, including its Live video streaming tool.

The NPR report cites the deposition of Reagan Maher, who worked in safety at the company in the early 2020s, addressing the fallout from a damning 2022 Forbes story about child exploitation on the platform. Maher said she informed senior leaders at the company that kids aged 13 to 15 were accessing features meant for adults, such as monetized live video.
More from CNET

A spokesperson for TikTok told CNET in an email that the information in the NPR report was “clearly cherry-picked at the behest of trial lawyers and used to inaccurately rewrite our history and mislead the public about our commitment to youth safety and how our platform works.”

TikTok also said that NPR ignored “numerous documents and resources” that would demonstrate how the story’s claims mischaracterize the platform’s features. The spokesperson stated that the company has spent significant amounts of money on safety and introduced over 50 default protections for young users, including Family Pairing tools for parents, and that it was steadfast in its “commitment to the well-being of our community.”
Child-safety reckoning on tech platforms

TikTok is one of a growing group of major tech platforms that have faced lawsuits, scrutiny from parents and financial penalties over how they regulate the safety of younger users. Others include the gaming platform Roblox, AI companies such as OpenAI, streaming video services like Google-owned YouTube and social media companies such as Meta.

Online dangers like predators, cyberbullying and inappropriate content aren’t the only risks for kids. Tech companies are also facing lawsuits for making their platforms addictive and harmful to young users. In August, Meta agreed to an $18 billion settlement over those issues in a landmark lawsuit brought on by multiple US states.

TikTok and its parent company, ByteDance — which still holds a stake in the company despite some government-mandated divestment to the US for its American operations — were sued in 2024 by the Department of Justice over violations of child privacy laws, resulting in a $400 million settlement. Last month, TikTok settled a $100 million lawsuit in Alabama and agreed to limit daily child usage in the state.

The NPR report shows not only that TikTok was made aware of these problems by its own staff. It also reveals that the company — among other alleged violations of the law — may have directly profited from the sexual exploitation of minors. Youth were reportedly rewarded with gifts online that could be converted to cash, with TikTok earning a cut of those profits.
Devastating, but predictable
Child-safety advocates told CNET that the NPR report exposes safety gaps in the way platforms such as TikTok were designed.

“These court documents are nothing short of devastating, but for those of us fighting child exploitation every day, they are tragically predictable,” said Michael Medoro, chief operating officer of Childhelp, which focuses specifically on online safety.
Medoro said that active monitoring, the elimination of safety loopholes and stronger age verification will require cooperation between tech leaders, advocates and law enforcement.

According to Shanna Marzilli, CEO of Plan USA, an advocacy group for girls that is part of Plan International, the TikTok documents confirm what young people, especially girls, have been saying for many years. “Online spaces are not safe for them,” she said.

Marzilli said that young people are clued into the idea that tech companies can’t protect them. In a research study conducted among US young people aged 10 to 19, only 14% of them trust social media companies to take sexual harassment and assault seriously.
“Voluntarily implemented parental controls and self-reported age limits are demonstrably ineffective when platforms leave these structural loopholes open,” Marzilli said.

articles.headline: Meet the California multimillionaires demanding the billionaire tax become law

body: The increasingly cantankerous fight over California’s proposed billionaire tax is now pitting the .01% against the .001%, as a group of multimillionaires call out their even richer counterparts for not paying more taxes.

Disney scion Tim Disney, Men’s Wearhouse founder George Zimmer and former San Francisco congressional candidate Saikat Chakrabarti — a mere centimillionaire as one of the founding engineers of Stripe — are among more than 40 wealthy Californians who signed an open letter urging voters to approve Proposition 40, a proposed one-time tax on the state’s billionaires.

“As multimillionaires, we’re willing to do our part,” the letter says. “It’s past time for billionaires — our thousand millionaire cousins — to do theirs.”

The letter by Patriotic Millionaires and Tax the Ultra-Rich Now supports a 5% tax on the net worth of billionaires who lived in California as of Jan. 1, 2026. Others who signed on include documentary filmmaker Matthew Cooke and virtual reality pioneer Jaron Lanier.
Chakrabarti has been particularly pointed in defending the labor-sponsored wealth tax, dismissing warnings that it would send California’s richest residents fleeing for other states.

“I think the disappointing thing is how few of the people who have made their wealth because of everything California has given them are willing to do the bare minimum to keep 3.4 million people from losing Medicaid,” Chakrabarti told The California Post in a text message.

“My thoughts on Sergey Brin, Eric Schmidt and others is this: all of you are probably going to make about 30% returns on your money this year, based on what returns for billionaires have been over the last several years. You won’t even notice a 5% wealth tax — you’ll still be richer next year than you were this year.”
He added, “But over 3 million Californians will have their lives changed. Do you really want your legacy to be that you fought tooth and nail against that?”
Disney, a filmmaker and author, cast the measure as a response to federal health care cuts and a fight over whose interests government serves.
“Prop 40 is about dignity, decency, and fairness,” Disney said in a statement.
He argued that the tax would help prevent millions of Californians from losing health care following cuts under President Trump’s “One Big Beautiful Bill.”
A spokesperson for the billionaires group fighting the wealth, Building a Better California, delcined comment Tuesday.
The millionaires group released findings from a YouGov poll of California millionaires that they said showed 57% support for Prop. 40.
Roughly 60% of those polled supported higher taxes on people with extreme wealth if the proceeds went to state health and education programs, according to a news release.
Another 56% said they would not leave California if asked to pay a little more in taxes, while 78% agreed billionaires have too much influence in state elections.
The release did not include the survey’s sample size, field dates or margin of error.
“If there’s a price tag on our beaches, our mountains, our piers, our cable cars, our forests, and our state parks, we’re proud to pay it,” the letter says.
Rather than letting the billionaires eat their cake, the millionaires seem ready for a food fight.

body: Trump says he will have spent $400m to support Republican candidates in midterms
Donald Trump said that he will have spent $400m supporting Republican candidates in midterm races by the time election day rolls around on 3 November.
The staggering amount will be spent through his political operation and aligned Super Pac, Maga Inc.

It is my Great Honor to do so on behalf of the Republican Party, which has done so much to bring our Country back from the Edge of Oblivion,” he wrote on Truth Social.

He cited his belief in the Republican party, but also the riots that have swept through France, as his reasons behind the spend. A reminder, Trump has repeated baseless claims that the demonstrations, which have descended into chaos and seen thousands arrested, are the result of mass migration.

Trump loyalist and rightwing influencer Laura Loomer tore into the Department of Justice on Tuesday, saying the agency was belittling veterans, who were exposed to contaminated drinking water at a Marine Corps base decades ago, with “lowball” settlement offers.

“This is a political disaster waiting to happen. Let’s be clear: Democrats are 100% going to weaponize this against President Trump and try to hurt him with veterans heading into the midterms in two weeks,” Loomer wrote in a X post, blaming associate attorney general Stanley Woodward Jr.
In a thinly-veiled rebuff, attorney general Todd Blanche appeared to suggest Loomer’s diatribe was financially-motivated.
“You should be transparent with your followers, and you are dead wrong about Stanley,” he responded on X.
“We love our veterans and we want to get these cases right. Find a different obsession other than going after one of DOJ’s best fighters.”
Loomer shot back, saying Trump wanted to fire Woodward, but took pity on him “because his lefty wife is divorcing him,” she claimed.

Some outlets, including Bloomberg, reported earlier this year that Harmeet Dhillon, an assistant attorney general in the DOJ’s civil rights division, would be promoted to Woodward’s post. She was not.
Trump's use of an antisemitic slur for a second time draws belated, indirect criticism from ADL

The Anti-Defamation League, which calls itself the world’s “leading anti-hate organization”, founded in 1913 “to protect the Jewish people”, denounced the use of the term “shylock” as antisemitic on Tuesday, without explaining that the slur had been used one day earlier by Donald Trump in a speech in Kansas.

The ADL’s brief social-media post made no mention of Trump at all and offered no explanation as to why the group found it necessary to explain, today, that anyone equating an avaricious person to Shylock, the villainous Jewish moneylender in Shakespeare’s Merchant of Venice, is using an antisemitic trope.

“The term ‘Shylock’ is rooted in a longstanding antisemitic stereotype,” the ADL posted on X but not its other social media accounts. “Regardless of intent, its use can reinforce harmful tropes about Jews and normalize language that has long been used to target the Jewish community.”

Critics who accuse the ADL of using accusations of antisemitism selectively, to attack people who are critical of Israel, suggested that the Jewish-American civil rights group was going easy on Trump because of his support for Israel.

Matt Duss, a former foreign police adviser to senator Bernie Sanders, the most prominent Jewish American politician, responded to the ADL’s failure to mention Trump by suggesting its president would have been more direct had someone else used the slur. “If a Democrat said it Jonathan Greenblatt would be knocking people over to get in front of a camera to condemn them by name, but it was Trump so it’s just a general public service announcement,” Duss wrote.

In 2014, after then vice-president Joe Biden described people who take financial advantage of American service members as “shylocks”, the Anti-Defamation League’s national director accepted his apology and called the remarks “a teachable moment”.
Trump’s use of the slur, at a rally in Kansas on Monday night, came just one day after he had endorsed Israel’s prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, on Monday, ahead of Israel’s elections.

Trump invoked the antisemitic stereotype as part of his defense of the Republican senator, Roger Marshall, a doctor who has been criticized for filing lawsuits against more than 700 patients with outstanding bills, leading to 18 of them being arrested.
The president began by claiming, falsely, that Marshall had been required by law to take legal action over unpaid bills, even one for just $101.

Marshall, Trump told supporters at a rally outside Wichita on Monday, “was given a bum rap because he was mandated by law to request strongly, money owed from patients. You’re not allowed not to do it. You have to, by law, go after those people.” There is, in fact, no such law.

Turning to Marshall’s critics, including his Democratic rival, Adam Hamilton, who featured some of Marshall’s patients in a campaign ad, Trump said: “they made it like, oh, he was some kind of a Shylock-type guy.”

“If he didn’t make these requests, he would be breaking the law,” Trump said again, repeating the falsehood he based his defense on. “He would have been breaking a very strong criminal law, and he would be subject to criminal arrest and liability,” the president claimed, falsely.

Trump’s use of the antisemitic slur came 15 months after he was made aware of its meaning when he used it at a rally in Iowa. Speaking on 3 July 2025, Trump Trump told supporters that eliminating the taxes on inherited family farms would save farmers from “going to the banks and borrowing from, in some cases a fine banker, and in some cases shylocks and bad people”.

The day after that Iowa rally, the ADL called the president’s use of the term “very troubling and irresponsible”, but Trump claimed ignorance when he was asked by a reporter if he had intended to use the word “shylocks” to refer to Jews.

“No, I’ve never heard it that way,” Trump replied then. “To me, a shylock is somebody that’s a, uh, a moneylender at high rates. I’ve never heard it that way. You view it differently than me. I’ve never heard that.”

Donald Trump said that he will have spent$400m supporting Republican candidates in midterm races by the time election day rolls around on 3 November. The staggering amount will have been spent through his political operation and aligned Super Pac, Maga Inc. The president will continue his campaign blitz with a rally in Greenville, North Carolina on Tuesday.

Beyond Washington, Trump’s special envoys – Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner – wrapped up a meeting with Nordic leaders and Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Oslo. The Ukrainian president said that the talks covered security guarantees, among others, and he hopes to hear Russia’s response tomorrow. Witkoff is set to head to St Petersburg on Wednesday to relay to the new peace proposals discussed with Ukraine to Moscow.

Zelenskyy also said that US intelligence sharing with Ukraine is working again, after sustained disruptions. Earlier, the Ukrainian president said he had a “substantive conversation” with US secretary of state Marco Rubio.

Meanwhile, Rubio told reporters in India today that “there has not been some deliberate political directive to go out and harm Ukraine”. He called the assertion that people in Ukraine are dying because the US is denying them information “scandalous” and “outrageous”. However, in an interview with CNN, representative Eugene Vindman, the Democratic congressman from Virginia, slammed the secretary of state’s comments. “He [Rubio] is lying and so is the president when they say that they are not restricting intelligence in violation of the law,” Vindman said.

And Trump continued to blame the riots in France on mass migration, without providing any evidence. “It’s an immigration problem. You have people that poured into France, and they were also unchecked, unvetted, like with Biden when he was doing. We don’t do that,” Trump said. Even though French authorities have not tied the upheaval to immigrants, that hasn’t deterred the president from insisting that similar chaos would be the US’ fate if Democrats win control of Congress in the upcoming midterms.
Also in the Oval Office today, Mehmet Oz – the director of the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services announced that the health department would be deferring $1.2bn more to California.
This comes after the Trump administration already paused almost $1bn in Medicaid funding to the Golden state in July.

“They just got the note, and we’re doing that because the growth of personal care services in California,” Oz told reporters on Tuesday. “That one little area where you’re paying someone to carry groceries upstairs for your mom, which many of you would carry groceries upstairs for your mom for free, I would think. But in California, they’ll pay you a lot of money for it, and it’s actually run by the counties. But California has been growing that program 24% in the last three years.”
Once again, Trump launched into a racist attack against Democratic congresswoman Ilhan Omar, and the Somali-American community.

This comes after the justice department launched a raid on the Minnesota representative’s Washington DC home. Reports citing sources familar with the probe said the search earlier this month was related to a criminal fraud investigation concerning Omar’s immigration paperwork. Omar’s father filled out that paperwork when she was a child. The raid has been met with widespread condemnation, particularly so close to the midterm elections.
However, Trump today doubled down.
“I think she’s a sick, a very dishonest person, but who hates our country. And she comes from a country that is essentially not even a country, Somalia. It’s a real shit house,” he said.

“Somalians vote for her … Most of them shouldn’t be here. You know, they have like a 98 % unemployment rate. They don’t work,” the president added, an incredible statistic given the fact that the census doesn’t actually track the unemployment rate for Somali-Americans specifically.

Donald Trump was not optimistic about whether peace talks appear to be back on the table ahead of Steve Witkoff’s meeting in St Petersburg, Russia tomorrow (following his summit with Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Nordic leaders in Oslo).

“Russia is a big machine. They just keep grinding forward, and that’s what they’ve done. They’ve taken a very large piece of land, and you know you can say that Ukraine is doing well or poorly, but the land gets bigger and bigger all the time, week by week,” Trump said, before repeating his insistence for Zelenskyy to cut a deal.

“We have given tremendous amounts to Ukraine. We’ve got nothing back, other than high diesel,” Trump said, without acknowledging that the price of diesel and gasoline jumped at the beginning of the Iran war in February. “We want Zelenskyy to make a deal. He can make a deal … In my opinion, it’s just really just going to get worse.”
On France, the president once again said – without providing any evidence – that the riots are due to mass migration.
“It’s an immigration problem. You have people that poured into France, and they were also unchecked, unvetted, like with Biden when he was doing. We don’t do that,” Trump said.

However, the French authorities have not tied the upheaval to immigrants, but that hasn’t deterred the president for insisting that the chaos would be a fate the US is destined for if Democrats win control of Congress in the upcoming midterms.
Donald Trump announces incentive program for people to report fraud, after conservative YouTuber Nick Shirley's allegations

In the Oval Office, Trump announced an incentive program for people to report fraud, in honor of conservative YouTuber Nick Shirley – who, you may remember, posted a video last year alleging fraud by daycare centers servicing Minneapolis’s Somali American community.
The video, initially posted in December, resulted in a deluge of anti-immigrant and anti-Somali content across social media, including in Truth Social posts by Donald Trump.
In July, Fahima Egeh Mahamud, the CEO of the daycare center that appeared in Shirley’s video, pleaded guilty to wire fraud and conspiracy to defraud the US.
Under the administration’s proposed program, people who submit information through that results in a fraud conviction could receive up to $30,000.
In the Oval Office today, Trump presented Shirley, 24, with a check for $10,000 for his work.
Trump says he will have spent $400m to support Republican candidates in midterms
Donald Trump said that he will have spent $400m supporting Republican candidates in midterm races by the time election day rolls around on 3 November.
The staggering amount will be spent through his political operation and aligned Super Pac, Maga Inc.

“More than 300 Million Dollars has already been spent on Advertising, Direct and Indirect Voter Contact, Rallies, Rally Arenas, Telerallies, Get Out the Vote Programs, Election Integrity, and more. It is my Great Honor to do so on behalf of the Republican Party, which has done so much to bring our Country back from the Edge of Oblivion,” he wrote on Truth Social.

He cited his belief in the Republican party, but also the riots that have swept through France, as his reasons behind the spend. A reminder, Trump has repeated baseless claims that the demonstrations, which have descended into chaos and seen thousands arrested, are the result of mass migration.
Kansas has not sent a Democrat to the Senate since 1932 – does Adam Hamilton have the courage, brain and heart to cause an extraordinary upset?

Just two years after Donald Trump won Kansas by 16 points in his fight to regain the White House, Republicans in the state are scrambling to retain their dominance. The battle for one of its two seats in the US Senate is too close to call, setting the stage for a potentially extraordinary upset.
Some recent polls even put Democrat Adam Hamilton on course for a historic victory. Kansans have not sent a representative of the party to the US Senate since 1932.

On the campaign trail, Hamilton regularly points to one of his state’s most famous residents: Dorothy from Wizard of Oz. Recalling a visit he made to Liberal, Kansas, and its Oz museum, he asks the audience to recall what Dorothy’s companions on her journey need. The lion needed courage, the scarecrow a brain and the tin man a heart.

Washington needs more of all three, he says, and he can deliver it. He decided to run for office after seeing the Trump administration act in ways that were “not good or kind or compassionate or humble”, Hamilton – in the energetic cadence of the pastor he is – told a crowd of business leaders in Topeka on Friday. He was waiting for Roger Marshall, the state’s Republican incumbent senator, to stand up for his state and its people.

“I would have arguments with Roger Marshall in the shower. He was not in the shower with me,” Hamilton joked. “And I would just say, Roger, please stand up for your people. You were not hired to be a spokesperson for the White House. You were hired to fight for your people.”

Hamilton’s role as senior pastor of the country’s largest United Methodist congregation comes with name recognition and speaking skills. But Marshall’s liabilities as his opponent – namely, the fact he sued hundreds of his patients for unpaid bills, resulting in the arrests of dozens of them – have contributed greatly to Hamilton’s prospects of flipping the seat.

Electorally, he’s trying to win over independents and Republicans, calling himself an independent-minded Democrat. It would be valuable, he told the business leaders last week, for Kansas to have a Democrat like him and a Republican in Jerry Moran representing them in the US Senate – working both sides of the aisle.
Mike Bloomberg is donating $80m to Democrats ahead of the upcoming midterm elections.

Speaking to the New York Times on Tuesday, Bloomberg’s advisor Howard Wolfson said: “He believes in participation in our democracy. And obviously the scale of his participation, given his resources and his means, is greater than other people’s financially. But other people are participating in different ways.”
“He is of the view that resources matter in campaigns,” Wolfson said, adding that Bloomberg “expects a result.”

The outlet reports that the former New York City major, now 84-years old, is focused on securing a Democratic majority in the House of Representatives, with at least $50m of his doantion to be spent on House races.

In response to Bloomberg’s donation, House minority leader Hakeem Jeffries said: “Mayor Bloomberg played an incredibly instrumental role in the decisive midterm election in 2018. The extraordinary support from Mayor Bloomberg will once again help Democrats flip the House,” the outlet reports.

articles.headline: Robinson sparks 23-0 run as Pistons stun Celtics in NBA season opener
keyFacts: Duncan Robinson scored 15 of his 21 points in the fourth quarter to help the Detroit Pistons beat the Boston Celtics 121-113 in the NBA season opener on Tuesday.
The Detroit Pistons used a 23-0 run in the fourth quarter to overcome a deficit after trailing by as many as 22 points earlier in the game.
Paul George scored a game-high 38 points in his debut for the Boston Celtics, while Jalen Duren and Cade Cunningham each scored 22 points for the Pistons.
body: Duncan Robinson scored 15 of his 21 points in the fourth quarter as the Detroit Pistons reeled off 23 unanswered points to beat the visiting Boston Celtics 121-113 in the NBA’s regular-season opener on Tuesday afternoon.
Jalen Duren and Cade Cunningham scored 22 points apiece for the Pistons, who led the Eastern Conference with 60 wins last season.
Javonte Green came off the bench to score 19 points in 18 minutes, while Ausar Thompson added 11 points, 11 rebounds and five assists.

Paul George scored a game-high 38 points on his Celtics debut. Payton Pritchard and Derrick White scored 17 points apiece, but Jayson Tatum was held to 13 points on six-for-23 shooting, although he contributed 11 assists.
The Celtics led by 13 at halftime thanks to a second-quarter surge. Detroit held a 39-35 advantage early in the quarter before Boston reeled off 15 unanswered points.
George scored the Celtics’ final eight points of the half as Boston took a 58-45 lead into the break.
George showed no signs of cooling off in the third quarter, hitting three three-pointers in a 52-second span to give Boston their biggest lead at 72-50.

Green entered the game shortly afterward to slow George down. He not only did that but also gave Detroit an offensive spark, scoring 11 points in the quarter, including three three-pointers, as the Pistons pulled within three in the closing seconds.

George opened the fourth quarter with a layup to give Boston a 90-82 lead. The Celtics soon stretched their advantage to 12 points, but Detroit began another comeback, sparked by a three-point play from Thompson.

Robinson scored 11 straight points to pull the Pistons within one at 99-98. He then set up a three-pointer for Green before Duren converted a three-point play. Robinson hit another three-pointer with 5min 13sec remaining to put Detroit ahead 107-99.
Green capped the 23-0 run with another three-pointer, extending the Pistons’ lead to 112-99 with 3min 33sec left.
Boston rallied to within four points, but Green made two free throws with 6.7 seconds remaining to seal Detroit’s opening-day victory.

articles.headline: French government extends curfews after riots sweep across the country
keyFacts: French authorities extended curfews and increased police presence after riots resulted in over 2,500 people taken into police custody.
Protests that began with students and teachers demanding better schools have expanded into broader demonstrations against living costs.
Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu promised a massive police deployment ahead of scheduled demonstrations on Oct. 24.
body: French authorities are extending curfews and increasing the police presence in public spaces as President Emmanuel Macron's government after rioters torched buildings and looted thousands of businesses this weekend.
But addressing the problems that have brought students and workers for the last five weeks will be a tougher proposition.
Protesters better schools and relief from rising living costs, while the government faces mounting debt and a fractured parliament that makes even passing a budget difficult.
More police and curfews

Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu promised a "massive" police deployment Tuesday ahead of the next demonstrations scheduled for Oct. 24. The announcement followed Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez's acknowledgment that authorities had underestimated the unrest and lost control in some cities during Saturday's protests.

More than 2,500 people into police custody by Monday evening, Justice Minister Gérald Darmanin said, after violence that included the burning of a historic town hall in Limoges, a city in central France.

Overnight curfews have been imposed around Paris' Place de la République and Les Halles shopping district, with restrictions also introduced in Lyon and other cities. Paris and Lyon reported no major incidents Monday night, and authorities are extending the measures.

In an address Sunday, Macron distinguished between the peaceful protests for better schools and working conditions and the rioters who he said hijacked those protests, saying that the government would both listen to the protesters' demands and punish rioters. He blamed "radical far-left groups" and "criminals" for the violence and said that "those who sought to bring down the republic will be held accountable."
Political gridlock and financial pressure

The protests began in mid-September when high school students and teachers in the suburbs of Paris called for changes to overcrowded classrooms, deteriorating buildings and teacher shortages. They have since drawn in trade unions and Yellow Vest activists, a French grassroots organizing group, becoming a broader movement against high living costs and declining public services.

The government has offered some concessions. On Oct. 8, the Ministry of National Education announced plans to deploy more than 3,000 substitute teachers to high schools most in need, and authorized several hundred additional hires.

But worsening financial pressure and political gridlock make more comprehensive changes more difficult. France's public debt stood at nearly 3.6 trillion euros at the end of June, equivalent to 119% of its annual economic output, according to the national statistics agency.

The government expects this year's deficit to reach 5.4% of economic output and is trying to reduce it to 5% in 2027. Interest payments alone are projected to rise by 12 billion euros next year, to 91.2 billion euros, further squeezing the money available for public services.

Macron's allies also lack a majority in the French parliament. This year's budget was adopted only in February, after the government pushed it through without a final vote on the bill, which survived two no-confidence motions.

An Ipsos poll conducted Oct. 7-8 put Macron's approval rating at just 15%. A September Ipsos poll put , National Rally party, well ahead of the field, with 33% to 35% support in different first-round matchups. Former Prime Minister Édouard Philippe and Jean-Luc Mélenchon, leader of the far-left party La France Insoumise, were among those vying for second place.
In April, France will hold presidential elections to choose a successor to Macron, who cannot run for a third term.

articles.headline: AfD's Alice Weidel to unveil plan to cut EU powers — report
keyFacts: Germany's AfD co-leader Alice Weidel is expected to present a policy paper aimed at reducing European Union powers and budget.
Politico reported the party plans to demand sweeping reforms before threatening a German referendum on EU membership if demands are rejected.
The AfD hopes to implement these European Union policies following the next federal elections in 2029.
body: Alice Weidel, the co-leader of Germany's far-right AfD, is expected to present her party's policy for the EU at the European Parliament on Wednesday.
According to a report from news outlet Politico, the AfD policy paper on the EU does not seek to exit the bloc or the eurozone at first.
The party rather wants to downsize the EU's powers and budget.
What's in the AfD policy paper?
Instead of direct European Parliament elections, the AfD would like to see delegates appointed by national parliaments.
The AfD would also limit the scope of the European Commission to purely administrative tasks and supplant the European Court of Justice with an arbitration tribunal.
The far right party would threaten to slash Germany's contributions to the EU budget.

Germany under the AfD would seek exemptions from EU regulations regarding issues such as migration and social policy. The AfD may also seek opt-outs of other areas such as agriculture and financial policies.
If the EU would not bend to the AfD's demands for reform, the party would then seek a German referendum on EU membership.

A referendum would be unrealistic, as it would require a constitutional amendment to the German Basic Law to take place. An amendment would require a two-thirds majority vote in both the Bundestag and upper house Bundesrat — an extremely high threshold to meet.
AfD eyes victory in next federal elections in 2029
The AfD hopes that it can implement its EU policies in 2029, when the next German and European elections will take place.

Recent German federal election surveys show the AfD in first place but it would have to form a coalition with another partner to establish a ruling majority government. That's difficult when other parties such as the conservative Christian Democratic Union refuse to have any cooperation with the AfD as part of a "firewall" policy.
